name: Windows
overview: Scripture uses the imagery of windows to reveal moments of divine intervention, human observation, and vulnerability. In Genesis, the 'windows of heaven' opened to unleash the floodwaters, demonstrating God's sovereign judgment, while Noah's opening of the ark's window signified hope and new beginnings. Other passages depict windows as vantage points for watching and waiting, such as the mother of Sisera looking out anxiously (Judges 5:28) and the wise man observing through his casement (Proverbs 7:6). Additionally, windows symbolize exposure to judgment and frailty, as Jeremiah describes death entering through windows into palaces, and Ecclesiastes portrays the darkening of those who look out from them, reflecting the frailty of life and impending decline.
